steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Biological: genes, neurotransmitters (dopamine, serotonin), brain localisation, evolution, twin/adoption studies

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cognitive: schema, mental models, computer analogy, cognitive neuroscience (fMRI, PET)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Behaviourist: Pavlov (classical: NS->CS), Skinner (operant: reinforcement/punishment), Bandura (SLT: observation, modelling)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Psychodynamic: Freud (id/ego/superego, psychosexual stages, defence mechanisms), unconscious motivation

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Explain how the biological and cognitive approaches differ in explaining depression --- Solution: Biological: genetic predisposition, serotonin/noradrenaline deficit, hippocampal atrophy -> treatment: SSRIs, ECT. Cognitive: Beck's negative triad (self, world, future), cognitive distortions, schema -> treatment: CBT (challenge thoughts). Biological = reductionist, medical; Cognitive = mental processes, empowerment

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Compare SLT vs operant conditioning | Evaluate twin studies for nature/nurture | Explain Freud's defence mechanisms with examples

steps.title: Lesson plan
steps.body: Starter (5 min): Recall prior knowledge of approaches and perspectives with quick questions. Teaching (15 min): Work through each of the learning objectives, explaining principles step by step. Key points review (5 min): Revisit the key points together, confirming understanding. Worked example (10 min): Model the example question: Explain how the biological and cognitive approaches differ in explaining depression. Solution: Biological: genetic predisposition, serotonin/noradrenaline deficit, hippocampal atrophy -> treatment: SSRIs, ECT. Cognitive: Beck's negative triad (self, world, future), cognitive distortions, schema -> treatment: CBT (challenge thoughts). Biological = reductionist, medical; Cognitive = mental processes, empowerment Practice (10 min): Students attempt the practice ques
